description: Artificial turf, dog runs and putting greens in Calabash, NC, planned around the Town's 25% impervious line, its plastic landscaping rule and its ditch rules.
h1: Artificial turf in Calabash, NC, planned around the Town's 25% impervious line.
lede: Calabash runs its own stormwater review, and how turf is counted can decide whether you need an engineer. Free visit, ground checked, written price.
wins: Know where your lot sits against the 25% line
Keep turf off the Town's ditch and roadside strip
Approve the layout before any ground is moved

answer.question: Do I need a Town permit for artificial turf in Calabash, NC?
answer.answer: Expect to. The Town's stormwater chapter requires a Town Storm Water Permit for land of one acre or less, and an engineered plan above 25% impervious surface on a house lot. Ask the Town whether that 2004 text is current.

blocks.h2: In Calabash, the hard share of your lot decides how much paperwork the turf needs.
blocks.takeaway: Add up the roof, driveway, walks and patio first: on a house lot, more than 25% impervious surface means an engineered plan. Ask the Town how it counts turf and base.
paras: Calabash wrote its own stormwater rules into Chapter 53 of the Town Code, adopted August 10, 2004. Section 4 applies it to every property owner and to all construction, including improvements to existing homes. Section 9 sends construction that needs no state certification to Section 8.2.

Section 8.2 is short. A Town Storm Water Permit is required for land of one acre or less. On a residential lot, more than 25% impervious surface requires an engineered stormwater plan. Every commercial job needs an engineered plan, and land over one acre is regulated by the State.

Add up what is already hard on your lot: roof, driveway, walks and patio. Near a quarter of the lot, the way the turf is counted can decide whether you need an engineer. The chapter counts compacted soil, gravel roads and recreation facilities as built-upon area, and leaves out slatted wood decks, pool water and new types of pervious paving material.

State law has since spoken to turf. As WithersRavenel quotes it, G.S. 143-214.7D(b)(6) says turf made to drain through its backing, installed to the maker's specifications over a pervious surface, is not built-upon area for stormwater programs. Our guide to built-upon area on both sides of the state line covers the rest. The Chapter 53 we read is the version recorded in 2004, so ask the Town whether Section 8.2 is still current and how it will count your turf and base.

blocks.h2: Calabash already bans landscaping that sheds rain like a sheet.
blocks.takeaway: The Town's ban on solid plastic and vinyl landscaping never names turf, and turf that drains through its backing is built to let rain through. Keep the maker's drainage information with your permit papers.
paras: Section 7 of Chapter 53 sets standards for homes that are already built. Its second rule says no landscaping using impervious materials such as solid plastic and vinyl will be permitted, and that property owners must remove any put down before the chapter took effect. After giving notice, the Town can fine $200 for each violation.

The rule never names artificial turf. It targets surfaces that stop rain reaching the ground, and turf that drains through its backing, over a base that lets water pass, is built to do the opposite. Keep the manufacturer's drainage information with your permit papers in case the Town asks.

Section 9 adds a rule for land outside a subdivision: no change of the terrain or drainage without prior approval from the Town. If the layout raises, lowers or reroutes the ground on a lot like that, get the approval before we start.

blocks.h2: Your front lawn may cross onto Town ground before it reaches the road.
blocks.takeaway: The grass strip you mow out front may be Town right-of-way. Check your survey, and keep the turf, base and any drain pipe out of the ditch unless the Town authorizes it.
paras: Chapter 54 of the Town Code, recodified March 8, 2011, covers streets, rights-of-way and the ditches beside them. Section 54.25 bars anything placed on a street right-of-way unless the chapter allows it. It is unlawful to obstruct a drainage ditch so it impedes the flow of water, to place anything across a ditch without the Town's prior authorization, or to block a ditch right-of-way so maintenance equipment cannot move.

Anything left there stays at your own risk. If it is not removed within a reasonable time after the Town gives notice, the Town removes it at your expense, and the penalty is $100 for each day. Section 54.22 sets $200 a day for blocking a culvert, ditch or drain so water cannot flow over or under a street.

Section 54.42 shows how far Town ground reaches. Town staff mow from the pavement edge to the center of the shoulder ditch, and from there to the property line no more than two times a year, and the policy covers Town property only. So the grass strip you mow may not be yours. Check your survey, and keep the turf, its base and any drain pipe out of the ditch and the right-of-way unless the Town authorizes it.

blocks.h2: Zoning, flood, inspection, CAMA and stormwater all sit with the Town.
blocks.takeaway: The Town, not the County, handles zoning, flood, inspection, CAMA and stormwater here. If your address is Calabash but you’re not sure you’re inside town limits, confirm with the county first.
paras: Brunswick County's municipal jurisdictions table lists the Town, not the County, for flood, building inspection, CAMA, zoning and stormwater in Calabash. Town office hours are 8:30 AM to 4:30 PM, Monday through Friday. The same table sends Shallotte's building inspection to the County, so one town's process is no guide to the next.

The Building Inspector handles the Storm Water Permit. A denial can go to the Planning Board, then to the Town Council. If you are cited under Section 8.2, Section 12 gives you 30 days to file a written appeal with the Storm Water Appeals Board, made up of Planning Board members.

Near the water there is one more step. Construction under one acre that reaches into a State-defined Area of Environmental Concern needs a CAMA minor permit from the Town's Local Permit Officer. Chapter 53 names coastal wetlands, estuarine waters, estuarine shorelines and public trust areas among those most applicable to Calabash. Ask whether your lot touches one before the layout is final.

Hickmans Crossroads carries a Calabash mailing address, but a mailing address is not the same as Town limits. Brunswick County's municipal jurisdictions table assigns the Town, not the County, for zoning, flood, building inspection, CAMA and stormwater inside Calabash - it says nothing about where that line runs, or about Hickmans Crossroads by name. If your address is Calabash and you are not sure your lot sits inside Town limits, ask Brunswick County which jurisdiction, Town or County, covers your parcel before the layout is final.

Calabash's own communities add another layer beyond the Town or County rules above. Kingfish Bay is a private, gated community on the Calabash River, and Devaun Park is a Traditional Neighborhood Design community on the Calabash River. Calabash Station, Coastal Club of the Carolinas, Hunters Trace and Meadowlands are also named communities in the Calabash area. If your lot sits in any of these communities, start with Brunswick County's jurisdictions table to see whether the parcel falls inside Calabash town limits, where the Town's stormwater, ditch and impervious-surface rules above apply, or in unincorporated Brunswick County, where County rules apply instead. Either way, your community's association still decides what it will approve on an individual lot. Get its current covenants or architectural guidelines, and its sign-off, before the layout is final.

blocks.h2: Add a retaining wall or a shed and Article 11 applies as well.
blocks.takeaway: A sloped green may need a retaining wall: three feet or less skips setback rules, taller needs a building permit. Sheds can cover up to 10% of the lot, 5 feet from any line.
paras: A green on a sloped yard can call for a retaining wall. Calabash's Article 11 table of area, yard and height, last amended January 12, 2022, frees a wall of three feet or less, measured from the lowest ground to the top, from setback and yard rules. A taller wall needs a building permit.
Accessory buildings may cover up to 10% of the gross lot area and must stand at least 5 feet from any lot line, which matters if a garden shed joins the plan.

Our free visit measures the area and checks the ground and where water meets the street. You approve the custom layout first, with a base built for your soil. Take that drawing to Town Hall, and see our backyard putting greens if a green is part of it.

servicesNote: Choose a lawn, a dog run or a backyard putting green, and we'll set its edges inside your property line and clear of the ditch.

faq.q: Does artificial turf count toward the 25% limit in Calabash?
faq.a: That turns on how the Town reads its 2004 definition alongside state law. Ask the Town how it will count your turf and base, bring the manufacturer's drainage information, and get the answer in writing if your lot is close to the line.

faq.q: Can I lay turf on the strip between my yard and the street ditch?
faq.a: Not until you know where your property line is. Ground on both sides of a shoulder ditch can belong to the Town. Mark the line from your survey, and ask the Town before any turf, base or pipe goes near the ditch.

faq.q: What should I ask Calabash Town Hall before turf goes in?
faq.a: Give staff your address and the layout, then ask three things: whether the job needs a Storm Water Permit, how the turf will be counted, and whether your lot touches an Area of Environmental Concern.

faq.q: I have a Hickmans Crossroads address near Calabash. Which rules apply?
faq.a: That depends on whether your parcel sits inside Calabash Town limits, not on the mailing address. Brunswick County's jurisdictions table sets the Town's authority for zoning, flood, building inspection, CAMA and stormwater inside Calabash; it doesn't name Hickmans Crossroads or mark the boundary. Confirm which jurisdiction covers your address with Brunswick County before the layout is final.
